steps.body: A **rational number** is any number that can be written as a fraction a/b of two integers (b ≠ 0). That includes whole numbers (5 = 5/1), negatives (-2 = -2/1), and familiar decimals (0.5 = 1/2). Every rational number, in decimal form, either stops or repeats forever.

widget.prompt: Which of these numbers is rational?

choices.feedback: Yes! 0.5 = 1/2, a ratio of two integers — that makes it rational.

choices.label: nothing — only whole numbers are rational
choices.feedback: Whole numbers ARE rational (5 = 5/1), but so are fractions and terminating or repeating decimals — the category is bigger than just whole numbers.

choices.label: only fractions with a small denominator
choices.feedback: Size of the denominator doesn't matter — 7/1,000,000 is still perfectly rational.

steps.body: Why do rational decimals always stop or repeat? Long division only ever produces remainders smaller than the divisor — so dividing by 3, the only possible remainders are 0, 1, or 2. Eventually a remainder must repeat, and once it does, the digits after it repeat too.

explanationVariants: 1/3 = 0.333…, the digit 3 repeating forever — 0.3 alone is only a rounded approximation.
Dividing 1 by 3 never reaches a remainder of 0, so the 3s never stop.

choices.label: 0.333…, repeating forever
choices.feedback: Right — the 3s never stop.
0.3 is close, but it's a rounded approximation, not the exact value — the 3s keep going forever.
Still just a rounded approximation — 1/3 never terminates.
That misplaces the decimal point entirely — 1/3 is less than 1.

steps.body: See why the remainder forces a repeat.

authoredStages.title: Step 1
authoredStages.body: Divide 1 by 3: it goes in 0 times, remainder 1. Bring down a zero to make 10. Then 10 ÷ 3 = 3, remainder 1 — the SAME remainder as before.

authoredStages.title: Step 2
authoredStages.body: Since the remainder is back to 1, the very next step is identical to the previous one — so the digit 3 repeats forever.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — a repeating remainder locks in a repeating digit.

steps.body: Which of these will terminate (stop) rather than repeat?
explanationVariants: 3/4 = 0.75 exactly — the division reaches a remainder of 0 and stops.
Only 3/4 hits a remainder of zero; the others cycle through nonzero remainders forever.

widget.prompt: Which fraction's decimal STOPS instead of repeating?

choices.feedback: Right — 3/4 = 0.75 exactly, then it stops.
1/3 = 0.333… repeats forever — it never stops.
2/3 = 0.666… repeats forever.
1/6 = 0.1666… — after the first digit, the 6 repeats forever.

steps.body: Which fraction produces a REPEATING decimal?
explanationVariants: 1/4, 1/2, and 1/5 all hit a remainder of 0 and stop; 1/3 never does.
Only 1/3 cycles through nonzero remainders forever — the others terminate.

steps.body: Rational numbers are a/b fractions, and their decimals always terminate or repeat.
takeaways: Every rational number's decimal either stops or repeats a block forever.
A repeating remainder in long division is what forces the repeating digits.
0.333…, 0.4545…, and 0.875 are all rational — two repeat, one terminates.
steps.teaser: Next: predicting which fractions terminate and which repeat — before you ever divide.
